entries.detail: Hayward ADU fees re-verified in the Adopted Master Fee Schedule FY2026-27 (effective July 1, 2026, read live November 10): the park impact fee for ADUs of 750+ sq ft falls from $3,812 to $3,379 (Park Impact Fee – Residential, item 43a; the whole table moved down — studio $3,789, 1-bedroom $5,931, 2-bedroom $10,699, 3-bedroom $18,685, 4+ bedroom $25,991), and the ADU sewer connection charge rises from $5,295 to $5,825 per unit (September 1, 2026 column). The same schedule lists an ADU housing review fee of $158 (1–4 units $474, 5+ units $790) — confirmed in the document, not yet encoded as a fee row. The homepage 750 sq ft cliff example is corrected to $3,379. Hayward now has 3 rows (3 verified).
entries.headline: Hayward FY2027: park impact fee $3,812 → $3,379; ADU sewer connection $5,295 → $5,825

entries.detail: Source-URL correction, no fee amounts changed: FI-308 (Laguna Beach USD school fee) and FI-433 (Paramount USD school fee) source URLs move from http:// to https:// — the plain-http documents time out while the https versions load (Paramount via a 301 redirect). The homepage school-fee chart now excludes Chula Vista: its only verified school row is FI-269, the Sweetwater Union HSD share ($3.01/sq ft, grades 7-12), with the Chula Vista Elementary share unverified, so the $2,408 shown was a high-school portion only. The cheapest five are now Laguna Beach $1,640, Pasadena $1,792, Sierra Madre $1,792, Paramount $2,376 and Simi Valley $2,560; the headline spread ($1,640 → $9,968, 6.1×) is unchanged. entries.headline: Source URLs http→https for Laguna Beach and Paramount school fees; Chula Vista leaves the homepage chart

entries.detail: San Luis Obispo County (unincorporated): the Nipomo Community Services District verification-of-service letter ($389, 2025-26 Miscellaneous Fee Schedule Res. 2023-1681, Code Sec. 2.04.070(A)) is verified — the district's own form lists 'New Accessory Dwelling Unit (ADU)' as a service type, and the schedule was re-fetched live November 10 (same 77,285-byte PDF, $389 unchanged; water lateral inspection $430 and sewer lateral inspection $281 also unchanged). The letter is area-tagged 'Nipomo' so it enters only the Nipomo area schedule, never the county-wide total; the same tag is added to the district's other four rows (capacity $0 verified, water lateral $430, sewer lateral $281 and 1-inch meter $1,013, all still unverified as conditional). 'Nipomo' (Nipomo CSD) is a different service area from the county's 'Nipomo (CSA 1)' wastewater row — a parcel pays one provider's rows, never both. entries.headline: Nipomo CSD verification-of-service letter $389 verified (Nipomo area)

entries.detail: Lakewood's two verified school-fee rows were summed into a single $6,680 figure ($8.35/sq ft) on the homepage chart, the /fees/lakewood/ page and the calculator — but Long Beach USD and Paramount USD are both unified (K-12) districts, so a parcel pays one district's fee, never both. The rows now carry area tags (Long Beach USD, Paramount USD), following the Carlsbad pattern (FI-534–537) and the Vacaville precedent. No rows added for them; the Lakewood post already states the four-district split in prose.
entries.headline: Lakewood school fees split into exclusive areas: Long Beach USD $5.38, Paramount USD $2.97 (a parcel pays one, never both)

entries.detail: San Luis Obispo County (unincorporated) gains 10 water/sewer provider rows. One verified: Golden State Water's Los Osos service area charges $0 in water connection/capacity fees for an ADU sharing the existing service — current Rule No. 16 (Advice Letter 1996-W, effective May 21, 2026) provides one standard connection up to 2 inches at no charge per single-family parcel, its connection-fee table lists Bay Point only so Los Osos has no fixed connection fee, and a qualified ADU is not new residential use for connection fees or capacity charges unless built with a new single-family dwelling (Gov. Code Sec. 65852.2(f)(3)(A); Advice Letter 1946-W background). A separate ADU service, if requested, is billed at actual installation cost on a quoted estimate — no published fixed fee. Nine rows stay unverified, all from the county Public Works 'Sewer and Water Connections (Will Serve)' page read live November 9: county service-area connection fees for a single-family residence — Cayucos (CSA 10A) water $8,100, Shandon (CSA 16) water $2,800, Santa Margarita (CSA 23) water $2,725, Nipomo (CSA 1) wastewater $2,000, Oak Shores (CSA 7A) wastewater $2,075, San Luis Obispo Country Club (CSA 18) wastewater $2,500 — plus 1-inch meter fees for Cayucos $350, Shandon $575 and Santa Margarita $260. Each carries an area tag so a parcel pays one service area's rows, never the sum. ADU application is unconfirmed for all nine: the county page lists single-family residence fees only. The county's Los Osos capacity fee of $23,852 is NOT duplicated here — it is already CSD-01 in the pending cycle296 branch, and the county's live Will Serve page now lists it as the current fee (with a September 2022 Board of Supervisors hearing on the establishing resolution), which the daily routine can use to flip CSD-01 to verified. S&T Mutual Water Company (Sunset Terrace, Los Osos) publishes no connection-fee amount online — not found, not encoded. In this branch the county has 12 rows (2 verified).
entries.headline: SLO County water/sewer providers: Golden State Water Los Osos ADU $0 verified; county CSA connection fees recorded

entries.detail: Marin County (unincorporated) gains 2 verified state-tax rows (port of the November 5 draft, re-verified live November 9 from the county Community Development Agency's 'Understanding Your Permit Fees & Charges' page): the Seismic Motion Instrument Program (SMIP) tax at 0.01% of the value of the proposed improvements for residential occupancies ($0.50 minimum, CA Public Resources Code Sec. 2705(a)) and the Building Standards Commission 'green' tax at 0.004% of the same value ($1.00 per $25,000 of improvements, $1.00 minimum, CA Health and Safety Code Sec. 18931.6(a)). Unlike the county's 10%/6% surcharges verified in the previous cycle, these two are percentages of improvement value, so the encoding is dimensionally correct — but feeCalc still skips them while the county has no valuation basis on file, so they carry no dollar total yet (the same treatment as Diamond Bar's verified percentage rows). The county now has 4 rows (4 verified).
entries.headline: Marin County state taxes verified: SMIP 0.01% + green tax 0.004% of improvement value

entries.detail: Marin County (unincorporated) gains 2 verified surcharge rows (port of the November 5 draft, re-verified live November 9 from the county Community Development Agency's 'Understanding Your Permit Fees & Charges' page): the Planning Surcharge Fee at 10% of the building permit application + issuance fees (Ord. 3372) and the Technology Enhancement Fee at 6% of the same sum (Marin County Code Sec. 19.04.032(d)(6)). Both are percentages of the permit fee, not of valuation, and are encoded as such; feeCalc skips them while the county has no valuation basis on file, so they carry no dollar total yet (the same treatment as Diamond Bar's verified percentage rows). The building permit base fee itself stays unverified: the county's Permit Base Fees page still publishes ranges only (Single Family Dwellings $3.87-$13.32 per sq ft; Attached/Detached Accessory Uses $3.09-$12.49), placement inside the range is unpublished, and no county page states which row a detached ADU falls under — so no fixed 800 sq ft permit fee can be stated. The county now has 4 rows (4 verified).
entries.headline: Marin County permit surcharges verified: Planning 10% + Technology 6% of permit fee

entries.detail: Marin County gains one verified row: the Marin Municipal Water District water capacity charge for an ADU is $0 when the Code §11.56.050(h)(3) conditions are met, verified live today on the district's Code of Ordinances (Ord. 469, 3/18/2025): no new or separate water service and no capacity charge for one ADU per lot if the newly constructed ADU is at most 1,200 sq ft detached (50% of the primary dwelling if attached) on a lot with an existing single-family home and existing water service, the ADU or the home is owner-occupied, both meet the water-efficiency standards, and the applicant has been a continuous district customer for at least one year. It applies only to parcels in the MMWD service area (central/southern Marin), so it is area-tagged and never summed with the North Marin Water District Facilities Reserve Charge lines. An ADU that fails the conditions pays a charge proportionate to its drainage fixture units — no published schedule, so that amount is not encoded. Marin County now has 3 fee rows, all verified.
entries.headline: Marin County: MMWD water capacity charge verified at $0 for a qualifying ADU (Code §11.56.050(h)(3))

entries.detail: Marin County gains one verified row: the North Marin Water District Oceana Marin sewer connection charge for an ADU is $15,000, verified live today on NMWD Regulation 109 (June 2023 revision, still current on nmwd.com): the regulation charges $30,000 per single-family dwelling and 50% of that charge for an accessory dwelling unit. It applies only to parcels in Improvement Districts OM-1/OM-3 (Oceana Marin, Dillon Beach area), so it is area-tagged and never summed with the Novato Sanitary or Las Gallinas sewer lines. The FY2023-24 annual sewer service rate ($1,374 per equivalent unit, ADUs at 50%) is recurring and is not encoded. Marin County now has 3 fee rows, all verified.
entries.headline: Marin County: Oceana Marin ADU sewer connection verified at $15,000 (NMWD Regulation 109)

entries.detail: North Marin Water District Regulation 1 (effective December 6, 2022, still the current revision on nmwd.com — re-verified live November 9, 2026) sets the Facilities Reserve Charge for a second dwelling unit / ADU up to 1,200 sq ft and up to 50% of the primary dwelling at $7,640 in the Novato service area and $5,580 in the West Marin service area, corroborated by the district's 2022 Facility Reserve Charge Study (Tables 3 and 6) and its July 19, 2023 response to the Marin County Civil Grand Jury. Both rows are area-tagged (a parcel is in one service area only) and capped at 1,200 sq ft; above that the full single-family charge applies ($28,310 Novato / $20,660 West Marin, not encoded). This resolves the three-way figure conflict: the October matrix's $5,580 for Novato was the West Marin figure misapplied, and the Grand Jury report's $8,675 appears in no district document (the pre-amendment Novato ADU charge was $10,000 per the district's March 7, 2023 board agenda) and is treated as a stale secondary figure. The FRC is a connection/capacity charge, so SB 1117 does not change it; meter, service-line and reimbursement-fund charges are additional and not encoded. Marin County now has 4 fee rows (all verified).
entries.headline: Marin County: North Marin Water District ADU capacity charges verified (Novato $7,640; West Marin $5,580)

No. 2023-136) says an ADU is not a new residential use for capacity charges, except a detached ADU built with a new dwelling — re-read verbatim live November 9 from the district's online code book (Municode, version Apr. 3, 2024). The Intent-to-Serve $1,497 application is not encoded: ADU intake is the Verification of Service letter, not Intent-to-Serve. San Luis Obispo County now has 10 fee rows (2 verified).
entries.headline: San Luis Obispo County: Los Osos + Nipomo CSD connection rows added (8); Nipomo ADU capacity $0 verified

entries.detail: San Luis Obispo County (unincorporated) gains 11 Road Improvement Fee rows, all verified (port of the November 6 draft, re-verified live November 9 from the county's published Road Improvement Fee Schedule, effective March 1, 2026 — the live PDF is byte-identical to the November 6 copy). Each RIF area's ADU fee is the schedule's own arithmetic: cost per peak-hour trip x the ADU trip generation rate 0.41 pht/unit, per Note 5 ('Residential Secondary Unit (or ADU) 750 square feet and greater will be calculated using a flat rate based on proportion of the median ADU and median SFD (per Gov. Code 65852.2)'). Avila Valley $12,732 x 0.41 = $5,220.12; North Coast A $720 x 0.41 = $295.20, B $1,225 x 0.41 = $502.25, C $1,566 x 0.41 = $642.06, D $723 x 0.41 = $296.43, E $348 x 0.41 = $142.68; Los Osos $3,895 x 0.41 = $1,596.95; San Miguel $7,471 x 0.41 = $3,063.11; South County Areas 1 and 2 $14,842 x 0.41 = $6,085.22 each; Templeton $10,456 x 0.41 = $4,286.96. The 11 areas are mutually exclusive area schedules — a parcel pays one area's fee, never the sum — so each row carries its own area tag and the fee page shows the verified total as a range across areas ($4,279 in North Coast Area E to $10,221 in South County at 800 sq ft, including the $4,136 SLCUSD school fee). At 750 sq ft or less the RIF is $0 under Gov. Code 66311.5(c) (the schedule's '750 and greater' wording is overruled by state law at exactly 750 sq ft). The flat RIF lines are SB 1117-uncertain in 2027 — the county has published no rule for how flat fees map to the excess-area rule, so no 2027 figure is computed. Subdivision-agreement fees and the State Route 227 corridor program (case-by-case) are not encoded. The county now has 13 rows (12 verified).
entries.headline: San Luis Obispo County Road Improvement Fee verified: 11 area rates ($143–$6,085 per ADU)

entries.detail: San Luis Obispo County (unincorporated) gains 12 fee rows (port of the November 6 draft, re-verified live November 9 from the county's published FY 2026-2027 Fee Schedule). Nine rows are verified: the seven Public Facilities Fee components for a Single Family ADU of 750-1,200 sq ft — Fire $1,130, General Government $580, Library $388, Park Development $832, Park Land $443, Sheriff $386, Admin Fee (2%) $75 — summing to the schedule's published ADU total of $3,834 (SFR row $8,657 for context; PFF table effective January 1, 2026; fire fees are paid directly to Templeton CSD for Templeton and Cambria CSD for Cambria, and Quimby-paid lots are exempt from the Park Land portion); plus Residential Single Family (R3) plan check $1.19/sq ft and inspection $1.59/sq ft including the 9.74% Technology Surcharge Fee ($952 + $1,272 = $2,224 at 800 sq ft; no ADU-specific building line exists, ADUs use the R3 rates). Three rows stay unverified: Fire-Rated New Construction - Small $1,957.76 (figure re-confirmed live today, but conditional — only when fire-rated construction is required, and the calculator has no conditional-fee mechanism); Lucia Mar USD school fee $5.17/sq ft (2024 vintage, FY 2023-24 annual report — no 2026 adoption of the $5.38 maximum found); Paso Robles JUSD school fee $5.17/sq ft (Resolution 25-19, adopted March 25, 2025 — the feeder-district split with Pleasant Valley / San Miguel JUSD is unconfirmed). The county now has 14 rows (10 verified), including the pre-existing SLCUSD school fee $5.17/sq ft (FI-191, verified) and Templeton USD $5.17/sq ft (FI-527, unverified). Verified total for an 800 sq ft ADU is $10,194 ($3,834 PFF + $2,224 building + $4,136 school). The seven flat PFF lines are SB 1117-uncertain in 2027 — the county has published no prorate formula for flat per-unit fees, so no 2027 figure is computed. Before the Lucia Mar / Paso Robles / Templeton school rows can be verified, all county school rows need mutually exclusive area tags (otherwise the calculator would sum $5.17/sq ft once per district).
entries.headline: San Luis Obispo County PFF verified: $3,834 ADU impact total + R3 building rates ($2,224 at 800 sq ft)

entries.detail: Monterey County (unincorporated) school fees are now split by district into three exclusive areas (a parcel pays one area's fee, never the sum). North Monterey County USD $5.17/sq ft verified (Resolution No. 2023-2237, adopted April 11, 2024 — the district's own resolution, re-verified live today; no 2026 adoption of the SAB $5.38 maximum was found, so the FY 2025-26 annual report due 2026-12-27 is the re-check target; 800 sq ft = $4,136). Carmel USD $3.78/sq ft verified (district's own Developer Fees page, live today, stating the current rate; Resolution No. 25-09, adopted May 14, 2025, effective July 13, 2025; 800 sq ft = $3,024). The existing Salinas-area SUHSD Level II $4.82/sq ft row (FI-504, 800 sq ft = $3,856) is area-tagged 'Salinas-area pockets' so it is no longer added to the other areas' totals. Verified school total for an 800 sq ft ADU is $3,024 (Carmel), $4,136 (North County), or $3,856 (Salinas-area). Ten draft rows stay unverified: the Article XIX building-fee band and its percentage items (plan check 32.5%, General Plan 15%, Technology 13% — text re-confirmed today, but dollar values depend on the unverified valuation band / permit fee, and the calculator's percentage method means percent of valuation, not percent of another fee; the $646 standardized-plan review applies only to the county's pre-designed plans, so it cannot be a flat row for every ADU); the four TAMC Regional Development Impact Fee zone bases (adopted-program ADU rule unverified; 2026 update maximums are proposed, not adopted); and the Cypress Fire Protection District $0.53/sq ft fire fee (ADU treatment unverified). Monterey Peninsula USD and other districts' pockets still have no verified rate.
entries.headline: Monterey County school fees split by district: NMCUSD $5.17 and Carmel USD $3.78 verified (three exclusive areas)

entries.detail: Stanislaus County (unincorporated) gains its headline impact fee, verified from two official county sources. The PFF Annual Report FY 2025 (Board agenda 2/3/2026) lists the unincorporated ADU total at $3,061 against the $10,171 single-family total, and Resolution 2021-0195 (Board agenda 5/11/2021) gives the formula: ADU fee = (ADU sq ft / primary sq ft) x single-family fee, lesser of the proportional amount or the ADU flat rate, with ADUs up to 750 sq ft exempt. Encoded as a dwelling-base line ($10,171 base, $3,061 cap, same Westminster pattern): at the 1,600 sq ft default primary, an 800 sq ft ADU prorates to $5,086, so the cap binds and the fee is $3,061; for a larger primary the fee is lower (3,600 sq ft primary: $2,260). SB 1117 converts exactly to $318 on the 50-sq-ft-above-750 basis at the default primary. The county ADU handout independently lists the same $3,061 ADU line and the 750 sq ft exemption. Four rows stay unverified: the Modesto City Schools combined school rate $5.17/sq ft (elementary $3.10 confirmed in the FY2025 report, high-school share inferred from the 60/40 split only, 2026 $5.38 adoption unconfirmed — the FY2025-26 annual report, due 2026-12-27, is the re-check target); septic upgrade $600 and demolition $450 (rates re-confirmed live in the handout, but mutually exclusive alternatives to the verified $900 new-septic fee — a parcel pays one of the three, and feeCalc has no alternative-group mechanism); planning review $102 first hour (rate re-confirmed, but conditional on departmental review being required). Stanislaus County now has 7 fee rows (3 verified).
entries.headline: Stanislaus County PFF impact fee verified: $3,061 at the 800 sq ft spec (prorated single-family base, capped)

entries.detail: Marin County (unincorporated) gains two verified sewer rows, split by service area (a parcel pays one district's schedule, never both). Novato Sanitary District area: sewer connection fee $12.20/sq ft verified — District Connection & Permit Fees and Charges effective 7/1/2026 set the full connection fee at $14,640 per family unit, and the District ADU page charges ADUs under 1,200 sq ft the proportion of ADU size to 1,200 sq ft, so an 800 sq ft ADU pays 800/1200 x $14,640 = $9,760. Las Gallinas Valley Sanitary District area (Santa Venetia, Marinwood, Lucas Valley): $0 connection/capacity fee for ADUs verified — FY2025-26 Final Budget (adopted June 18, 2025): 'ADUs are normally not subject to capacity or connection fees'. Both districts may still bill an annual sewer service charge (amount not in these rows). The November 5 draft's other 11 rows stay unverified: building-permit range $3.87-$13.32/sq ft (exact placement TBD), 10%/6% surcharges, C&D $50-$250, SMIP/green taxes, Roads Impact Fee 1% (ADU application unverified), NMWD Oceana Marin $15,000, NMWD Facilities Reserve Charge $7,640 Novato / $5,580 West Marin (2022 regulation; current rate unverified), and MMWD $0 conditional on owner-occupancy, 1-year customer status, and water-efficiency standards.
entries.headline: Marin County sewer fees verified by district: Novato Sanitary $9,760 (800 sq ft) vs Las Gallinas Valley $0

entries.detail: La Puente gains 18 fee rows (port of the November 5 draft, re-verified November 9 against the original sources, plus four LA County permit-fee lines). Twelve rows stay unverified: the five city planning lines (SPDR $892/$368 is discretionary review a ministerial ADU does not go through; planning final inspection $95 and zoning verification $200 are conditional/optional; landscape $850 is a deposit plus actual costs); Certificate of Occupancy (general schedule line only, cf. entries.headline: La Puente fee rows added (18): 6 county permit lines verified from the FY 2025-26 schedule; 12 rows stay unverified

entries.detail: The City of Vacaville's FY 2026-27 Service and Facility Rental Fees workbook (Planning Applications table) lists 'Accessory Dwelling Units' at $2,794 flat — the first row of the Planning Division fee table, found via the Planning Division Forms and Fees page. This closes matrix target #6, which was 'Not found' because the master fee schedule had not been located; ADUs are ministerial under VMC §14.09.270.040, but the city still charges the planning application fee (the ADU submittal checklist requires City Planner approval before the checklist is completed). The fee is verified, applies to the 800 sq ft spec scenario in full, and is not an impact fee, so SB 1117 (effective January 1, 2027) does not change it. Vacaville now has 14 fee rows (9 verified).

San Luis Obispo County (unincorporated) gains 2 verified water/sewer rows for the San Miguel area: San Miguel CSD ADU connection fees from the district's FY 26-27 schedule read live November 9 (effective July 1, 2026) — water $11.77/sq ft and wastewater $11.57/sq ft. At 800 sq ft that is $9,416 + $9,256 = $18,672. Both carry the 'San Miguel' area tag, matching the existing San Miguel RIF row, so a San Miguel parcel's verified total becomes $27,793 at 800 sq ft ($3,834 county PFF + $2,224 R3 building + $3,063.11 RIF + $18,672 CSD connections; no school fee is area-tagged to San Miguel yet — the San Miguel JUSD feeder split with Paso Robles JUSD is still unconfirmed). Connection/capacity charges are not impact fees, so the 750 sq ft exemption (Gov. Code 66311.5) does not apply to these two lines and SB 1117 leaves them unchanged. Not encoded: the district's 2024 Utilities Fee Schedule meter/installation figures — Resolution 2026-39 (adopted August 27, 2026) revised the utility fee schedule for water meter fees and other services, so the 2024 meter fee ($483 for a new 1-inch meter) is superseded and the revised amounts were not found in the published minutes; the Will Serve fee has no fixed amount in any published document. The county now has 45 rows (25 verified).

entries.detail: San Luis Obispo County (unincorporated) gains 5 Oceano Community Services District water/sewer rows, all area-tagged 'Oceano' so a parcel pays one service area's rows, never the sum. One verified: the district's Intent-to-Serve (Will Serve) application processing fee is $30 per structure or separate residential unit (application form revised 4/2025, which lists ADU as a project type). Four rows stay unverified, all from Ordinance No. 2006-1 read verbatim live November 9 (copy attached to the Feb. 14, 2024 board agenda): a new 5/8-inch water service connection fee of $675 installation plus $81.60 per front foot (minimum $4,755; larger meters higher, actual fee rises with frontage, and only when a new or separate service is installed); an additional connection fee of $1,000 per equivalent single-family dwelling; a water capacity charge set by formula only ($1,572 per ESFD in 1993, plus the SFR minimum bi-monthly charge times six each January 1) whose current dollar amount is not published and cannot be derived from public sources, so no amount is stated; and a water facilities inspection fee of $25 per unit for multiple units ($50 for a single-family dwelling — which row an ADU falls under is unconfirmed). The $1,000 fee and the capacity charge stay unverified for a substantive reason, not just missing paperwork: the ordinance defines an ADU-type unit as one ESFD, but Gov. Code Sec. 65852.2(f)(3)(A) says an ADU is not a new residential use for connection fees or capacity charges, and unlike Nipomo CSD or Golden State Water the district has no ADU provision stating which reading governs — the ordinance contains no 'accessory' at all. Not found, not encoded: the district's fixed sewer connection fee (connections are installed at the applicant's actual cost), meter costs under Ord. 2006-2 (cited in the Will Serve form, text not in the public index), and any South SLO County Sanitation District one-time connection fee (it levies recurring annual treatment charges only). The $1,500 Will Serve deposit is a deposit, not a fee. Oceano is in Lucia Mar USD, whose $5.17 school fee stays unverified pending its 2026 adoption check. In this branch the county has 48 rows (24 verified); the Oceano area's 800 sq ft verified total is $6,088 (county PFF $3,834 + R3 building $2,224 + Will Serve $30, school $0).
entries.headline: SLO County: Oceano CSD Will Serve fee $30 verified; water connection and capacity rows recorded

entries.detail: Lucia Mar Unified School District residential school developer fee verified at $5.38 per square foot, effective May 2, 2026 (800 sq ft: $4,304, up from $4,136 at the prior $5.17 rate). entries.headline: Correction: impact fees prorated to primary-dwelling size; Ontario areas no longer summed
entries.detail: Methodology correction, not a fee-schedule change. (1) Ontario: General City and Ontario Ranch are mutually exclusive area schedules (Res. 2025-010; Ontario Ranch DIF schedule eff. 7/1/2026) — a parcel pays one, not both. The old $96,171 cliff and $97,507 stack summed both areas at their full per-dwelling bases; both figures are withdrawn. At the 1,600 sq ft default primary, an 800 sq ft ADU now shows General City $18,798 + school $1,336 = $20,134, or Ontario Ranch $29,288 + school $1,336 = $30,624. The calculator has an area selector; jurisdiction and Fee Index pages show the range across areas. (2) Proration: cities that publish a per-dwelling base (not an ADU fee) now prorate as (ADU sq ft / primary sq ft) x base under Gov. Code §66311.5(c)(1)(B), with a new primary-dwelling input in the calculator (1,600 sq ft default, labeled as an assumption). El Monte's encoded $4,087 becomes base $10,217.26 (the $4,087 was the 800/2,000 example; at the default primary an 800 sq ft ADU pays $5,109; the SB 1117 note is recomputed to ~$319 at the same primary, and the Quimby exclusion is flagged unverified for 12/1 review). Lynwood's $2,756 becomes base $4,822.63 (the $2,756 was the 800/1,400 example; at the default primary an 800 sq ft ADU pays $2,411; two further schedule rows totaling $336.70 are under review for ADU applicability). Westminster is now min(prorated $17,179 base, $4,000 cap) instead of a flat $4,000. SB 1117 2027 conversions now cover dwelling-base lines too: ((sqft - 750) / primary) x base. Flat lines whose derivation is genuinely unpublished (including Hayward, a city-published ADU flat fee) stay marked 'conversion not published yet' and are never guessed. (3) Hayward park fee corrected $3,823 to $3,812 per the Adopted FY2025-26 Master Fee Schedule (eff. 7/1/2025); no FY2026-27 schedule was found as of 24 Oct 2026. Note: Fee Index figures previously shared with journalists used the old summed Ontario figures; they are corrected here and on the Fee Index page. Lines whose sources do not state a per-dwelling base are unchanged pending a second-phase source review.

entries.headline: Correction: 750 sq ft boundary updated to current law (SB 543)

entries.headline: Batch 18: 5 new jurisdictions, 12 verified fee items
entries.detail: Hemet, Sunnyvale, Marin County, Jurupa Valley, San Fernando (HCD ADU-permit ranks #105–109). Hemet's $8.647/SF DIF ($6,918 on 800 sq ft) is the matrix's steepest 750-sq-ft cliff; Jurupa Valley runs its own DIF program (Ch. 3.75); Marin County shows special-district fragmentation. Proportional-to-primary fees (Jurupa DIF/MSHCP) and track-ambiguous permit tiers held back as PARTIAL.

entries.headline: Batch 17: 5 new jurisdictions, 9 verified fee items
entries.detail: Pico Rivera, Saratoga, Mountain View, El Cajon, El Dorado County (HCD ADU-permit ranks #100–104). First East County San Diego and El Dorado County coverage; Mountain View's two-district school split ($5.24/sq ft) is the matrix's first; El Dorado County's $1,320 fire fee drops ~94% under SB 1117. Derived/proportional figures (Saratoga elementary $3.72, per-DFU sewer) held back as PARTIAL.

entries.headline: Batch 16: 5 new jurisdictions, 5 verified fee items
entries.detail: Davis, Temple City, Palmdale, Redwood City, Bakersfield (HCD ADU-permit ranks #95–99). First Yolo County coverage; Redwood City's $1.78/sq ft ADU sewer line is explicit in ordinance; Bakersfield's stacked 2016-dated DIFs held back as PARTIAL. Tracy, Hayward, Coachella, Rancho Cucamonga, Richmond (HCD ADU-permit ranks #89–94). Hayward's $5,295 sewer line is the matrix's first explicit 'all ADUs pay utilities' case.
